current.description: Nissi means island. A rock islet sixty metres offshore, soft sand, clear water. In winter the crowds disappear and the light changes. One of Europe's top 25 beaches.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. Promenade cafés often stay open.
current.description: Blue Flag sand, a swim-to islet, and five hundred metres of gentle shore. Winter walks are mild; the promenade cafés stay open. Protected from the north wind.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. No facilities on the sand.
current.description: A sheltered cove in Cape Greco. White sand, emerald water, cliffs on either side. Drop in from the coastal path in winter and you might have it to yourself.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. Tavernas often stay open.
current.description: Golden sand, calm waters, tavernas that stay open. Winter sunsets around five. Ideal for families; in winter it belongs to walkers and watchers.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. No facilities; pack water.
current.description: Protected coast on the Akamas. No sunbeds, no bars. Golden sand, turquoise water. In winter the turtles are gone and the beach is empty. Pack a picnic.
Wind and waves carved these caves. The limestone glows amber in winter light. Bring your camera and a wind layer. The crowds have gone.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. Cliff tavernas often stay open.
current.description: White cliffs above dark volcanic sand. Coves, tavernas, fresh fish. On a mild December afternoon you can sit outside with a blanket. One of the best winter lunch spots on the coast.
Roman villas buried for centuries, then brought back to light. Floor mosaics that rival Pompeii. The House of Dionysus, the House of Theseus. Winter light softens the stone. UNESCO.
Greco-Roman ruins on a cliff above the sea. Stand centre stage in the theatre and look out. Sunset around 4:30 in winter. Bring a wind layer.
Rock-cut tombs with Doric columns and atria. No royalty; the name reflects the grandeur. Winter light casts long shadows. Allow an hour. Pair with the mosaics and harbour.
Salamis was the largest city on the island. A theatre for fifteen thousand. Marble columns, baths, agora. North Cyprus; check access before you go. In winter you might have it to yourself.
The fairy-tale castle. Perched on a peak, the Queen's Window frames the sea. North Cyprus. The climb takes forty-five minutes. Clear winter days offer the best views.
Best ancient ruins in winter. City-kingdom above Limassol Bay. Summer turns the stone into an oven; December light is soft. Governor's Beach fifteen minutes away. Ruins in the morning, fish at lunch.
People lived here seven thousand years ago. Round stone houses, defensive walls, the island's oldest settlement. Winter mornings can be misty; dramatic for photos. UNESCO.

Winter visit: Commandaria wine was made here for eight hundred years. Square crusader keep, sugar mill ruins beside it. Thirty minutes; pair with a tasting at Zambartas (nearby) or Kolios (Paphos hills).

current.openingHours: Tue to Sun 8:30 to 17:00; closed Mon (from 1 Jul 2024)
current.description: Winter ruins: Aphrodite's sanctuary, quieter than the main Pafos mosaics. Best time to explore. Kouklia village wraps around the site. Stop for a coffee; the ruins are over your shoulder.

North Cyprus. Buffavento means Defier of the Winds—a ruined crusader castle on a ridge with the best winter views in the range. Forty-five minutes steep climb. St Hilarion to the west, the sea, the Mesaoria plain. More ruined than St Hilarion, fewer visitors. Verify border access from the south before you travel. Wear proper shoes.

current.openingHours: Tue to Fri 8 to 18, Sat 9 to 17, Sun 10 to 13; closed Mon
current.description: Best rainy winter afternoon in Nicosia. Nine thousand years of Cypriot history. Kourion Apollo, Neolithic figurines, Roman sculpture. Calm galleries. Central.

current.openingHours: Daily 9 to 17 (winter); may vary in north Cyprus
current.description: Abbey of Peace. Gothic cloisters, the Tree of Idleness in the village square. Durrell wrote about it. Winter concerts in the refectory. North Cyprus. The abbey at dusk.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sun 10 to 16:30; closed Mon and public holidays
current.description: Nicosia's story across five thousand years. Ancient Ledra, Venetian walls, independence. Free entry. Intimate galleries in the old town. Most visitors skip it; don't.
The castle guards Paphos harbour. Compact inside; half an hour is enough. The harbour walk in winter is the real prize. Sunset around five. Sit with a coffee and watch the light.

current.openingHours: Winter (1 Oct to 31 Apr): Mon to Sat 7:00 to 16:45, Sun 9:30 to 16:45 (DMT 2025). Confirm locally.
current.description: A 6th-century mosaic of the Virgin and Child. One of the oldest surviving Byzantine mosaics in the eastern Mediterranean. Most tour buses skip it. The village is quiet. The church is small, intimate. Allow forty minutes.

current.openingHours: Local museum Mon to Fri 8:30 to 16:00 (DMT 2025). Archaeological park hours vary — call 22 444818.
current.description: Ancient Idalion sprawls across two hills near Nicosia. Temple and palace remains, Aphrodite's sanctuary, and olive trees. Fewer visitors in winter; you might have it to yourself.

current.openingHours: Mon to Fri 8:30 to 16:00 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Sat and Sun.
current.description: Mycenaean and Phoenician Larnaca under the modern town. Kathari and Bamboula precincts, a temple of Astarte, and harbour works. Winter weekdays only; weekends closed. One of the few Department of Antiquities sites published as wheelchair-accessible throughout.

current.openingHours: Thermal baths vary; bridge and village always open
current.description: A Venetian bridge spans the river. Thermal springs bubble at the edge of the village. Stone guesthouses, mountain air. UN Best Tourism Village 2024. A soak in winter feels like a gift.

current.openingHours: Shops 9 to 18; some close for lunch
current.description: Lefkaritiko lace has been made here since the Venetians. Lacemakers sit in doorways; winter light catches the threads. Weekday mornings are quietest. Silver, cobbles, and the valley below.
Gateway to the Akamas. No high-rises, no neon. Tavernas by the harbour, fish that's fresh. Do Adonis or Aphrodite in the morning, lunch here. The pace is slow.

current.openingHours: Shops 9 to 18; monastery courtyard free; museum 9 to 17
current.description: The heart of the Krasochoria. Cobbled square, Holy Cross monastery, kafenions where zivania warms you up. Winter weekday mornings are quietest. Pair with Artemis and Tsiakkas.
Stone houses lean over the Karkotis River. Trout tavernas by the water, the Mill Hotel with a fireplace. Caledonia Falls is just up the road. Stay for lunch.
Artists breathed new life into Lania. Galleries, studios, and colourful shutters line the cobbles. Pair a morning here with an afternoon at Tsiakkas or Zambartas.
The Venetian aqueduct still stands. Citrus groves, Ottoman heritage, the smell of oranges in winter. Off the main track. Find the aqueduct first; the rest unfolds.

current.openingHours: Museum 9 to 16 (check for winter hours); workshops vary
current.description: Foini has made pottery since Byzantine times. Wood-fired kilns, the Folk Art Museum, and workshops where you can watch the wheel turn. A detour on the way to Platres.

current.openingHours: Church: key from museum; museum 9 to 16
current.description: On the road to Kykkos. Archangelos Michail holds vivid 15th-century frescoes. The key lives at the museum. Winter quiets the village; the church deserves an hour.
The hub of the Troodos. Artemis, Atalante, Caledonia all start nearby. Ski base in Jan to Mar; off-season the trails empty out. Trout tavernas, mountain air. Check conditions before you head up.

Krasochoria village with Commandaria tradition—not one of the fourteen UNESCO-named villages, but stone terraces and Hadjipavlou winery. Smaller than Omodos, quieter. Stop for lunch; the tavernas know how to cook. En route to Omodos and Koilani.

current.openingHours: Rose factory 8 to 17; tours by arrangement
current.description: The heart of Cyprus rose production. Rodostagma, loukoumi, preserves. The factory runs tours year-round; in winter they use the stored harvest. A bottle of rose water makes an ideal souvenir.
Fikardou was nearly abandoned; now it's a living museum. Stone houses, wooden balconies, and the Rural Life Museum. Twenty minutes to walk, an hour to feel. UNESCO.

Krasochoria village where Commandaria tradition runs deep. The wine museum traces five thousand years. December brings the Commandaria Festival. Even in January the tavernas are warm. Plan to eat. Then Vlassides for a tasting.
Same lace as Pano, often better prices. Fewer tour buses, more time to talk to the artisans. If Pano feels busy, slip down to Kato. The quality doesn't drop.
Vavla sits between Larnaca and Troodos; quiet lanes, olive groves, and guesthouses that offer silence and mountain views. The kind of place where you stay one night and wish for two.
Four painted churches, including UNESCO Panagia Podithou. The Cold River runs through. Key from the museum or café. Winter light is dim but the frescoes glow. Combine with Kakopetria.

One of the smallest wine villages on the island. Stand in the square and look west. On a clear winter day the light is magic. Vasilikon winery nearby. Stop before or after Adonis or Aphrodite. A coffee. A moment.
Shares the lace tradition with Lefkara but quieter. The workshops welcome visitors. A morning here, lunch in a taverna. Combine with Choirokoitia for a Larnaca hinterland day.
On the Limassol to Troodos wine route. Quieter than Omodos. Stop for a coffee; the kafenions know how to welcome strangers. Start here and work up to Omodos and Koilani, or do it backwards.
Above Omodos on the wine route. Fewer tour buses. Stone houses, a quiet square, and kafenions that locals actually use. Winter weekday mornings you might have the square to yourself.
Fifty-five kilometres from Nicosia at 860 metres. Eighty-five residents. Electricity arrived in 1970. A 17th-century stone church, the Aidonia nature trail, and two 19th-century stone bridges.
Ancient olive trees, some over a thousand years old. A traditional village square with backgammon-playing locals. Minimal WiFi, stubborn time capsule. The Paphos hills at their most authentic.
Before Polis, before the Baths of Aphrodite. A few hundred people. A kafenion. No tour buses. The views run down to the coast. Stop for a coffee if you're driving to Lara or the Adonis trailhead.
One of four Maronite villages. Arabic-speaking Cypriots who've been here since the 12th century. The church, the square, the sense of a culture that has survived. North Cyprus.

Golden stone houses, Byzantine chapels, and a 2.8 km nature trail through the Larnaca hills. Agrotourism guesthouses in restored village homes. Winter weekday mornings you might have the square to yourself. Dubbed the Little Tuscany of Cyprus—for the light on the stone, not the crowds.
Laona plateau village above Polis. Wide views, weaving and Rural Life museum, and the gateway to Gerakopetra crag. Fewer visitors than Omodos or Lefkara. A kafenion, a square, silence that holds.

Climber's village on the Laona plateau. Kafenion intel on road conditions, views to Polis bay, minutes from Gerakopetra crag. Winter weekday mornings: coffee, silence, and the road up to the boulders.
Cyprus's highest village at 1,380 metres. Apple orchards, mountain air, Prodromos Dam below. Mist, occasional snow, and a kafenion that understands cold cyclists and hikers.
Tiny Paphos Forest hamlet near Tzelefos bridge. Milia Eco Lodge restored stone houses; taverna food from the valley. Forest walks, river noise, and one of the quietest nights in Cyprus.
Mountain village on the Nicosia–Troodos road. Cool air, pine views, and a pace that slows you before Machairas or Kykkos. Winter stop for coffee when the capital feels too flat.
Laona plateau hamlet with sea views toward Polis. A few hundred souls, no tour buses, a church and a silence that holds. Stop between Droushia and Polis when the coast feels too busy.

Village on the Limassol–Platres road at 545 metres. Trimiklini Dam, a 1901 double bridge, and a Venetian relic in the Kouris bed. Most people drive through; winter cyclists and walkers stop for coffee and silence.
Marathasa Valley village with the oldest UNESCO painted church in the Troodos group (1280). Key from the village. Quiet valley base between Pedoulas and Kalopanagiotis.
Merged mountain village in the Paphos hills near Avakas Gorge. Organic wineries, gorge access, and views over pine-covered slopes. Quieter than Omodos; colder in winter.
Mesaoria foothill village gateway to UNESCO Panagia tis Asinou (1105). Byzantine frescoes of Constantinopolitan quality. Winter weekday visits often mean the church to yourself.
Lower Platres on the Kryos Potamos—quieter than the resort village upstream. Trout tavernas, forest walks, and Caledonia Falls access without the square crowds.
Evacuated village in the Paphos Forest—stone ruins, silence, and the trailhead to Roudias Venetian Bridge. Feels like an open-air museum. Remote; go with company and tell someone your route.
Hill village above Germasogeia Dam. Gateway to the Kyparissia ridge trail. Views over the reservoir and coast. Few visitors; kafenion pace.
Small Troodos forest village east of Kakopetria. Pine trails, frost in winter, and none of Platres square bustle. A base for Persephone and Almirolivado loops.

Commandaria village on the southern Troodos slopes. Stone lanes, almond groves, and a tomb dating to 700 BC. Quieter than Omodos; deeper in the wine valleys. Vine terraces and winter mist in the hollows.
Deep Commandaria country. Cooperative winery, cellar tours, and stone village quiet. Most visitors chase Omodos; Monagri makes wine without the performance.
Commandaria heritage village. Museum of wine tradition, terraced vines, and valley walks. Agios Georgios church anchors a hamlet that feels unchanged for centuries.

Pitsilia village in the eastern Troodos, southeast of Olympus. Chronias dam, pine forest, and zivania culture. Cooler than the coast; often snow-dusted in January. Starting point for eastern Troodos loops.
Pitsilia village on the road to Olympus. Stone houses, apple orchards, and views across the eastern Troodos. Quieter base than Agros for winter mountain days.
Limassol wine village on the Krasochoria route. Hadjipavlou and other wineries; stone architecture; views toward the coast. Less photographed than Omodos; more room to breathe.
Former mining village turned geopark gateway. Troodos Geopark Visitor Centre, recovering pine forest, and trails into ophiolite geology. Honest about industrial past; beautiful in winter snow.
Neolithic Tenta site and quiet village between Larnaca and Limassol. 7,000-year-old settlement; lace-making tradition; gateway to Vasilikon and Lefkara hinterland.
Mesaoria village with a five-domed Byzantine church and Xyliatos dam nearby. Agricultural plain meets foothills; quiet kafenion pace; winter birdwatching at the reservoir.
UNESCO Panagia tou Araka (1192) above the village. Among the finest Komnenian frescoes in Cyprus. Key from village; combine with Kakopetria or Agros for a painted-church day.
Mining heritage village with red lake views. Pyrite mine flooded in 1967—acid drainage colours the water. Industrial landscape turned strange beauty. View from safe points only; never enter the lake.
Kykkos crowns the Troodos; gold leaf, mosaics, an icon said to be by Luke himself. The drive through the pine forest is half the experience. The museum deserves an hour.

Neophytos carved his hermitage into the cliff in 1159. The Enkleistra cave holds frescoes he painted himself. Climb the steps, let your eyes adjust. The 12th century is right there. Paphos region stays mild in winter.

current.openingHours: Daily 8 to 12, 14 to 17. Call ahead after snow.
current.description: Fourteen hundred metres up. Active monastery, monks, a reverent welcome. The road from Platres can be snowy in Jan to Feb; call ahead. When it's open, the drive through the pine forest is beautiful. Dress modestly.
A hermit found an icon in a cave. The monastery grew around it. Dense forest, trails to nearby villages. Easy day trip from Nicosia. A morning inside, an afternoon walking. The silence is the gift.

current.openingHours: Daily 9 to 12, 15 to 18 (winter); museum 9 to 13, 14 to 17
current.description: The monks make wine. Buy a bottle; proceeds support the community. The red is surprisingly good. Views over the Paphos district. Combine with Vouni Panayia for a full day.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: Three churches share one timber roof in Kalopanagiotis. The frescoes span four centuries. The key lives at the village museum. Step inside and the walls speak. UNESCO for a reason.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: Near Lagoudera. Dated 1192. Among the finest Komnenian frescoes in Cyprus. Look up at the dome; the Pantokrator fills it. The key is kept in the village. Fewer visitors find it. That's part of the gift.

current.openingHours: Active convent; call ahead. Modest dress required.
current.description: Active convent above the sea near Cape Greco. Peaceful gardens. The coastal path runs nearby; visit the convent, then walk six kilometres of sea caves and cliffs. In winter the light is clear. The Mediterranean stretches to the horizon.

current.openingHours: Men: 8 to 12, 15 to 17; chapel at base: ask locally
current.description: Mountain of the Cross. The view from the car park alone is worth the drive. Men can enter the monastery; women the chapel at the base. The Mesaoria plain stretches for miles. On a clear day you see forever.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: Pedoulas. Frescoes from 1474. Blues, reds, gold. The Last Judgment covers one wall; Pentecost another. The key lives at the Folk Art Museum or the café. Small. Intimate. The 15th century surrounds you.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: St Nicholas of the Roof. The timber roof gives the church its name; a rare survival. Frescoes span six centuries. Above Kakopetria. Key from the Old Quarter. The trout tavernas by the river know how to warm you up after.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: UNESCO painted church in Moutoullas. 1280 frescoes; earliest of the Troodos painted church group.

current.openingHours: Tue to Sat 10:00 to 16:30, Sun 11:00 to 16:30 (winter 16 Sep to 15 Apr). Closed Mon. Confirm locally.
current.description: UNESCO church above Nikitari (1105). Comnenian frescoes of exceptional quality—Constantinople art in a Mesaoria foothill setting. Winter weekday visits often mean solitude in the nave.

current.openingHours: Check access—buffer zone area. Verify before visiting.
current.description: An abandoned village south of Nicosia. The church still stands; Byzantine frescoes survive on the walls. Ruined buildings, overgrown streets, and a silence that stays with you. Cyprus's divided past. Check access before you go—buffer zone nearby.

current.openingHours: Promenade always open. Shops and cafés seasonal hours.
current.description: Waterfront promenade, superyachts, and Mediterranean dining. The marina sits between the old town and the sea. In winter the crowds thin; the cafés stay open. A stroll here pairs well with Kolossi or Kourion. Urban Cyprus at its best.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. No ticket for the lake path.
current.description: Ramsar wetland beside the airport. Greater flamingos winter here from about November to March. A flat promenade and viewing points; Hala Sultan Tekke sits on the western shore. Free, always open, best at first light.

A leading sport-climbing crag on the Laona plateau above Polis. Hard sandstone at 600 metres; northeast-facing walls stay cool in summer. Over a hundred bolted routes from 5a to 8b+, plus boulders scattered on the hillside. Ineia and Droushia villages are minutes away. Dry winter days bring excellent friction; belayers need layers on shaded sectors.

The Laona plateau's boulder fields spread across four square kilometres around Droushia village. Sandstone blocks, steep roofs, and quiet hillside landings. Less documented than Gerakopetra's main wall but richer for explorers who like to wander. The village weaving centre and Rural Life museum are worth a stop on the way back.

A quiet bouldering valley in the Nicosia foothills. Small limestone blocks in a pine-scented gorge—exploratory terrain, not a polished crag. Locals know it; tourists rarely do. Good half-day from the capital when Troodos is snowed in and the coast feels too mild.

Quiet limestone boulders in the Pitsilia foothills east of Limassol. Smaller and less trafficked than the Laona crags. A handful of problems on good rock, pine shade, and views across the eastern Troodos. Combine with Agros or Machairas for a full Limassol hinterland day.

Modern indoor climbing and bouldering gym when the weather turns. Top-rope, lead walls, and a dedicated boulder cave. Winter rain or Troodos snow day? This is the fallback. Shoe rental available. Good for warming up before outdoor days or an evening session after village tastings.

Sea-cliff limestone on the island's eastern tip. Sport routes and trad lines above turquoise water. Winter is the window: cooler rock, fewer boats, calmer seas. Local operators run guided sessions. Even without ropes, the coastal path and sea caves reward a morning here.

Aphrodite's Rock and the limestone cliffs above the birthplace myth. Not a sport crag, but coastal scrambling and boulder problems near the shore. Winter sunsets are spectacular. Low crowds. Pair with the coastal walk toward Pissouri for a full active day.

Mountain roads and forest tracks around Platres and Troodos Square. Winter cycling is cool and quiet: Artemis road loops, Karvounas to Kakopetria descents, pine-scented climbs. Road and gravel options. Layer up; elevation brings cold. Cafés in Platres welcome muddy bikes.

Coastal and dirt roads through the Akamas peninsula. Latchi harbour to Baths of Aphrodite, Blue Lagoon viewpoints, and quiet village tracks. Winter mild on the coast. Gravel-friendly routes; some sections rough. E-bikes popular with local rentals.

Paved cycle path along the Limassol coast from the old port toward Germasogeia and beyond. Flat, family-friendly, winter sun. Connect to the dam loop for hills. Bike rental shops in the marina area. Evening rides when the light turns golden.

Glassy winter mornings in Latchi harbour. Kayak rentals and guided trips to the Blue Lagoon and Akamas sea caves when the sea is calm. Winter seas are cooler but often clearer; fewer boats. Wetsuit recommended Dec to Feb. Fish tavernas on the harbour for post-paddle lunch.

One of the world's top wreck dives. The ferry Zenobia sank in 1980 on her maiden voyage; she lies on her side at 16 to 42 metres. Winter visibility can be excellent when boats run. Certified divers only; Larnaca dive centres schedule trips year-round when weather allows—book ahead off-season. A bucket-list dive in the eastern Mediterranean.

Paddle into sea caves and arches on the Cape Greco peninsula. Guided kayak tours on calm days when operators run—call ahead off-season. Winter groups are small; the water is clear and the cliffs dramatic. Snorkelling from the kayak optional in mild weather.

Long flat beach and steady winter winds make Lady's Mile a local favourite for windsurfing and kitesurfing. Less crowded than summer. Wetsuit essential. Watch the salt lake flamingos on the drive in. Best on clear windy days Dec to Mar.

Natural sulphur springs piped into pools at this Miliou valley spa hotel. Thermal water at 28°C year-round. Day passes and treatments available. Winter is ideal: mist in the valley, warm water, quiet pools. Combine with Polis or Akamas hiking for a wellness day.

Limestone cliffs below the Kourion ancient theatre drop to Episkopi Bay. Not a bolted crag—a scramble zone where locals practice movement above the sea. Winter sunsets from the theatre are famous; the cliff path below is quieter. Check rock after rain.

Limestone coves and white cliffs between Paphos and Coral Bay. Snorkelling in clear winter water, coastal scrambling, and sea caves at low tide. Not the harbour-side White Rocks hotel—the wild coast near Agios Georgios Pegeias. Few tour buses in winter.

Cyprus's highest village sits beside a quiet dam and web of forest roads. Gravel loops through pine and golden oak, mist in winter mornings, snow dusting on the peaks. Cool, empty, and serious climbing—1,380 metres of elevation.

Linked wine villages on gravel and tarmac: Louvaras, Lofou, Omodos, Koilani. Rolling hills, vine terraces bare in winter, kafenion stops. E-bikes and gravel bikes love this loop. Quiet weekday riding; Omodos gets busier on weekends.

Remote fishing harbour on Cyprus's north-west tip. Pebble beach, crystal water, Dragon Cave kayak trips, and almost no winter crowds. The Tylliria peninsula feels like another island—slower, wilder, far from the resort coast.

Reservoir kayaking and SUP surrounded by Troodos foothills. Flat water, pine-scented shores, no sea swell. Winter mornings are mirror-calm. Local operators run sessions; the dam trail links to cycling and hiking loops.

Medieval single-arch bridge in the Paphos Forest. Moss, river noise, pine shade—a place that slows you down. Winter rains swell the Diarizos; mist hangs in the valley. Forest bathing, gentle walks, and one of Cyprus's most photographed hidden spots.

Steep limestone sport climbing ten kilometres from Paphos. Forty bolted routes from 6a to 8c on a south-facing wall—athletic overhangs and crimpy faces. Lower sectors dry fast after rain; winter is prime when inland crags are cold.

Twenty-one limestone boulder problems near the Episkopi sport crag. Low altitude, quick sessions, good winter sun. Less traffic than Laona. Combine with the main wall or a half-day when Gerakopetra is too far.

Exposed ridge above Germasogeia Dam with 685 metres of climb and panoramic Limassol coast views. Winter hiking and MTB when summer sun would be brutal. Natural cypress clusters, endemic flora, and silence above the reservoir.

Rolling dam roads and vineyard lanes around Trimiklini on the Limassol–Platres corridor. Double stone bridge, Venetian relics, and quiet climbing before the Troodos ascent. A locals' winter loop when the high mountains are snow-bound.
Forest roads around Xyliatos Dam in the Nicosia foothills. Quiet reservoir, pine shade, and linked villages—Peristerona, Agios Ioannis—on a mild winter loop far from the coast crowds.

Sheltered crescent bay for shore diving and snorkelling—sea turtles, ancient pottery on the seabed, calm entry when the open Med is rough. Prasinada to locals. Winter visibility can exceed summer; wetsuit essential.
Cliff-backed bay between Limassol and Paphos. PADI dive centre, white cliffs trail, and tavernas above the curve of the coast. Winter sunsets around five; mild when Troodos is cold.
Small Troodos village surrounded by pine—CTO trails, quiet forest bathing, and snow dust on nearby peaks in deep winter. Fewer buses than Platres; more silence.

Shallow reef dive and snorkel site off Paphos harbour. Roman amphorae encrust a cave roof at 12 metres—2,000 years of history above your mask. Green turtles and stingrays in winter when visibility clears.

UNESCO Global Geopark visitor centre in a restored mine school. Asbestos and chromite mining history, geological garden, copper furnace reconstructions. Forest trails radiate from the site—winter snow possible at this elevation.
Forest picnic site near Platres with tables under ancient plane trees. Stream noise, mountain air, and easy access when longer trails are snow-closed. Locals' winter lunch stop after a short walk.
Linked mountain roads through Agros, Alona, Polystipos, and Kyperounta. Vine terraces bare in winter, zivania distilleries, and views toward Olympus. Serious climbing; serious quiet.
Pine and golden oak above Tsada and Koili. Quiet forest roads for walking and gravel cycling. Minthis Golf overlooks the hills; the forest below stays wild and little visited in winter.
Reservoir and forest roads in the Nicosia District hills. Linked to the Potamia nature trail—easy cycling on quiet tarmac when Troodos is snowed in.
Quiet west Limassol coastline between Pissouri and Akrotiri. Cliff paths, empty shingle beaches, and winter light on white rock. No resort infrastructure—bring supplies.
Commandaria heritage valley. Ancient vine terraces, the Commandaria museum, and walks between stone-built hamlets. Winter light in the vines; zivania warmth in the kafenion.
Advanced shore dive at Cape Greco—Cyclops Cave drops beyond 30 metres for trained divers. Shallow caves nearby for snorkellers. Winter visibility and empty parking.

Limestone blocks in the Pitsilia foothills between Klirou and Arakapas. The east-corridor bouldering gap—exploratory problems on good rock, pine shade, views toward Papoutsa. Less polished than Laona; quieter than the capital valley.

Gravel and tarmac loop through Kalavasos, Tochni, and Zygi fishing harbour. Orange groves in the valley, mild winter sun, fish tavernas on the coast. Forty to fifty kilometres of rolling Larnaca hinterland—quieter than Troodos when snow closes the peaks.

current.openingHours: Open shoreline year-round. Schools and kit rental seasonal.
current.description: Shallow Larnaca bay with winter kite and windsurf when the wind cooperates. Calm days suit snorkelling and SUP; the wreck of the Zenobia lies offshore for divers. Finikoudes promenade ten minutes north. Mild eastern-Mediterranean winter coast—not empty, but far from summer crowds.

current.openingHours: Park open dawn to dusk. Visitor centre hours vary — call ahead off-season.
current.description: 840 hectares of pine and scrub on Nicosia's south-eastern edge. Twenty kilometres of walking trails, a sixteen-kilometre cycling route, lake, and botanical garden. Free entry; winter rain turns the paths quiet and green. The capital's quickest forest reset.

current.openingHours: Mon–Fri 10:00–16:00, Sat 11:00–17:00. Closed Sun except select dates.
current.description: Founded in 1988, Tsiakkas sits at 1,000 m in Pelendri, Pitsilia. Thirteen hectares of certified organic vineyards produce around 200,000 bottles of Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, and indigenous varieties. The terrace has heaters in winter; guided tours run Mon–Sat at 12:00 and 14:00. Reserve ahead—the family often pours.

Established in 1987, Vouni Panayia sits on a hill above Panayia village with views over Kannaviou Reservoir and the Troodos. After recent renovations it offers an educational film, traditional museum, and tasting room. Commandaria, dry whites, and robust reds from limestone-rich soils. The restaurant serves meals with valley views.

Founded in 2006 by Dr. Akis Zambartas, the winery focuses on indigenous varieties and environmentally friendly practice. Their Shiraz–Lefkada blend is a flagship, matured 12 months in oak. Three tasting experiences: Winemaker's Selection (€20), Seasonal Selection (€15), Wine & Canapés (€25). Winter hours 10:00–17:00 weekdays, 18:00 weekends.

current.openingHours: Winter (Oct–Feb): Mon–Sat 9am–3pm. Summer (Mar–Sep): Mon–Sat 8:30am–5pm. Sunday: private parties only (50+ guests).
current.description: Kolios sits on a mountaintop about a kilometre outside Statos Agios Fotios, towards Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery. At 3,000 feet, the family cultivates the largest organic Maratheftiko vineyard in Cyprus—no chemical fertilizers, only natural methods. Four generations have tended these vines. The underground cellar has oak barrels and a natural spring that keeps the humidity ideal for ageing. Guided tours at 12:30pm are followed by traditional meze lunch at 1pm, cooked by the owner's wife from local ingredients. Book one or two days ahead. The views over mountainous Paphos—pine-covered slopes, gorges, mouflons wandering the vineyards—reward the drive up.

current.openingHours: By appointment. Call for hours; road conditions vary Dec–Feb.
current.description: At 1,400 m, Kyperounta is among Europe's highest wineries by facility altitude. Established in the late 1990s, it began production in 1998. Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, and premium EPOS range benefit from slow ripening and mountain clarity. Three-level gravity-fed facility; underground cellar with 250 oak barrels. Call ahead—the road can close in snow.

Hilltop winery above Limassol with panoramic sea and vineyard views. The restaurant serves lunch most weeks; call ahead Nov–Mar. On mild winter days the terrace offers heaters and blankets. Sunset in December is around five—time a late afternoon tasting for the golden hour. Book ahead at weekends.

Founded in 2005 by Angelos Tsangarides, the estate has ~20 ha of certified organic vineyards and seven organic labels. Single Vineyard Xynisteri, Vasilissa Maratheftiko, Angels Rosé. No synthetic pesticides or chemical fertilisers. Stone-built tasting room with mountain views.

Founded in 1990 by Theodoros Fikardos, one of the first privately owned wineries in Cyprus. Vineyards in Pano Arodes and Choulou; grapes from Stroumbi, Tsada, Kathikas. Five ranges: Classic, Medium Sweet, Premium, Premium Limited Edition, Experiment. Terrace overlooking the vines.

current.openingHours: Mon–Fri 11:00–16:00 by appointment. Closed Sun & holidays.
current.description: Founded by Sophocles Vlassides (UC Davis), completed 2012. Unconventional architecture—represented Cyprus at the Mies van der Rohe Award 2015. Twenty-one hectares at 700–1,100 m. Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc; minimal oak, fruit-forward style. Rainbow tasting €7.50; 4×4 with cheese €18; Riedel experience €220.

current.openingHours: Winery 8:30–18:00, restaurant 10:00–16:00 in season; call ahead Nov–Mar.
current.description: Established in 1993 by the Kyriakides brothers. Sixteen hectares at 650–700 m; limestone and volcanic soils; sea breezes give a distinctive saline character. PDO Vasilikon Xynisteri (Laona Akamas since 2016), Ayios Onoufrios red (Silver 2014 International Challenge). Cellar, museum, restaurant, terrace.

Also known as Oenou Yi; founded 2017 by Christodoulos G. Vassiliades. At 800–1,000 m in the Krasochoria hills. Traditional Xinisteri (70%) and Mavro (30%), sun-dried; Commandaria gold medal at Thessaloniki 2021. Tours and restaurant (11:00–19:00) with village views.

Established 1983; first winery in Koilani. Run by Yiannoula and Ioannis Ioannidou. ~50,000 bottles/year from Mavro, Xinisteri, Muscat, Lefkada, Shiraz, Cabernet. Famous for Mosxatos sweet wines. Vineyard tour, tastings, local cheese and delicacies.
Owner Michalis Constantinides. Named after the Ezousa river; four hectares at 400 m. Indigenous varieties only—soils born of fire and time. ~52,000 bottles/year. Tasting room; book ahead.
Third-generation family winery in Pera Pedi at 770 m—Krasochoria village with Commandaria tradition. Traditional sun-dried grapes, long ageing. Stone cellar, mountain air. Call ahead for tastings.

Established 1996 on the foothills of Olympus. Maratheftiko, Xinisteri, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay. Tours through barrel room and bottling line. Professional staff, positive reviews. Near Troodos; road can be snowy Jan–Feb—call ahead.

Founded early 1990s by George Tripatsas. Three hectares; Maratheftiko, Shiraz, Chardonnay; natural farming. ~170,000 bottles/year. Two-level architecture, underground cellar, tasting hall overlooking Pitsilia. Artisanal cheese and charcuterie available.

Boutique family winery; four generations. Only Cyprus winery sourcing exclusively from own vineyards—17–28 ha at 400–600 m. Ungrafted vines, organic viticulture. Xynisteri, Morokanella, Spourtiko, Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi, Lefkada. Decanter and international awards.

Traditional village winery in Pachna at 750–800 m—Krasochoria foothills with Commandaria-style sweet wines. Generations of wine; Mavro, Xynisteri. Simple tasting room. Call ahead; drop-ins possible but winter hours flexible. Village tavernas nearby for lunch.

Founded 1992 by Yiannis and Alexia Christoudia (originally KRELAN). ~80,000 bottles from Xinisteri, Maratheftiko, Spourtiko, Cabernet, Muscat. Modern facility (2012) with barrel cellars. Fireplace in winter. Brunch with Cypriot cuisine; weddings and events.

Modern winery near Limassol with terrace views over the Mediterranean. Experimental blends and contemporary styles. ~20 min by car from the coast—combine with harbour lunch or Kourion. Terrace catches winter sun.

Small winery on the western Laona route in a restored stone building. Indigenous varieties, boutique production, intimate tastings. Stone walls hold warmth in winter; the pace slows. Western Laona has a different character—quieter, more remote. Combine with Chrysorrogiatissa or Vouni Panayia.

On the Akamas wine route with sweeping sea and vineyard views. Dry whites and rosés from the Kathikas hills—not Commandaria zone, but terrace views and Laona character. Kathikas village does lunch nearby. The drive through the Akamas wine villages is half the pleasure.
Elegant Xynisteri and Maratheftiko in the Krasochoria. Tasting room with Troodos views. Wine-and-cheese pairing worth booking. Koilani village nearby for lunch. Winter mountain light is sharp.

In the heart of Omodos. Cellar tastings, Commandaria aged the traditional way. Do the monastery and square first, then Komos. Village cafés do lunch. Ask to compare older and younger vintages. Winter visitors get the courtyard mostly to themselves.

Family-run in Vasa, one of the quieter Krasochoria villages. Their Lefkada is worth the drive. Warm welcome, mountain air. Call ahead; they appreciate the heads-up. Combine with Omodos or Louvaras for a full village day. The kind of place where someone pours and then sits down to talk.

Cooperative on the Laona route. Community-driven, traditional methods. Ask how it works; the story is part of the tasting. Agios Georgios village is quiet. Good for a slow afternoon. Call ahead. Groups welcome. It's the kind of place that shows you how wine holds villages together.

Silikou at 650 m—one of 14 villages authorised for Commandaria. Winemaking since Frankish times (~1200). Old vines, centuries of tradition. Commandaria from the heart of the zone. Off the main loop; fewer visitors, more room to breathe. Commandaria Museum nearby.
Small production in Miliou. Valley views from the terrace. Book ahead. Ideal for a quiet escape on the Laona route. The hills roll away; the Paphos hinterland has its own rhythm.

Five generations since 1913. Housed in a 200-year-old listed ancestral home in Vasa Koilaniou, meticulously restored. Eight hectares in Laona Krasochoria; Maratheftiko, Xynisteri, Cabernet, Merlot, Chardonnay, Viognier. Modern tech meets tradition. Wine Club for limited editions.

current.openingHours: 8:00–16:00 Mon–Sun in season; call ahead Nov–Mar.
current.description: Family-owned by Nicos Ignatiou and sons. Mataro, Xynisteri, Maratheftiko; Commandaria, liqueurs, Zivania. ~20 min from Paphos. Quality local wines—red, white, dry, semi-dry, sweet. Direct delivery of limited editions.

Organic and natural. Statos village, Laona plateau. Book the meze pairing; the cheese and olives make the wine sing. They're passionate about natural fermentation. Ask. The setting is peaceful. Plan to stay. Laona has a different vibe to the Krasochoria: quieter, more remote. Winter tastings feel like a gift.

Kilani village. Family estate. Their Lefkada has character; indigenous red, worth asking about. The Krasochoria hospitality is warm. Kilani is quieter than Omodos. Reserve for winter. Combine with Koilani and Vlassides for a full village day. The kind of place where someone pours and then sits down to talk.

Phinikas. Off the beaten path. Boutique Xynisteri and Maratheftiko, valley views from the terrace. The drive rewards. Call ahead; they run a small operation and appreciate the notice. Intimate. Quiet. The kind of tasting where you sit and the afternoon slips away. Western Laona has a different vibe to the main wine loop.

Monagri village, deep in Commandaria country. Cooperative production. Ask for the cellar tour; the story of how these villages have made wine for centuries is worth hearing. Groups welcome. Call ahead. Traditional Mavro, Xynisteri, and Commandaria. The kind of place where community and wine are inseparable.

Walk from the monastery square. Stone arches, village charm. One of the few Omodos wineries where you can drop in without a reservation. Commandaria, Xynisteri, Mavro. Do the village first; the cobbles, the kafenions; then Loukas for a tasting. Ideal for first-timers. The square is five minutes away.

Dhoros village. Mountain views. The fireplace is the draw. Book ahead and claim a seat. Their rosé is crisp even in winter; ask about it. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, the Troodos out the window. Cosy. Stay awhile. Winter tastings here feel like the reason you came.

Commercial production since 1988; moved to new premises 2009. Statos at 1,000 m in central Paphos mountains. ~200,000 L/year from 8 ha; Maratheftiko, Ophtalmo. Wines follow Byzantine and Roman traditions. Combine with Avakas Gorge—call from the car park when done; they're used to hikers.

Fourth generation. Koilani. Krasochoria hills with Commandaria tradition. Ask to see the cellar; it's historic, and the story is worth hearing. Krasas has been here for generations. It shows in the wine and the welcome. Book ahead. The cellar tour is the gift.

Agios Theodoros village. Small. Honest. The kind of place where the owner pours. Mavro, Xynisteri, and a sweet wine worth asking about. Call ahead. Off the main Commandaria loop, which means fewer visitors and more room to talk. The wine is straightforward. The welcome is real.
Right in Platres. Forest and vineyard views. Ski in the morning, Ambeli in the afternoon. Or Artemis trail, then taste. Lefkada has character. Winter tastings by the fire. Call ahead in season.

The Sergiou family makes wine in Skarinou, between Limassol and Larnaca. Indigenous varieties only: Xynisteri, Morokanella, Assyrtiko, Maratheftiko, and the Atypon blends. They often pour the tastings themselves and tell the story behind each bottle. Book ahead.

Founded 2013. Loucas Papaloucas, winemaker (ex-Kamanterena), blends tradition and innovation; minimal intervention. At 550 m, ~33 km east of Paphos. Chardonnay, Syrah rosé, Maratheftiko; Giannoudi, Promara, Orange Xynisteri. Labels use Linear B ideograms for 'wine.' Stone and modern architecture; cheese and charcuterie platters.

Oenou Yi (Ktima Vassiliades) established 2018. Private vineyards, some over 120 years old, on Afamis and Laona hills. ~250,000 bottles/year; indigenous Mavro, Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Lefkada, Promara, Vasilissa, Yiannoudi; Commandaria. Modern underground facility. 10:00–17:00 in season; call ahead Nov–Mar.

Family-run since 1995. ~55 ha in Kathikas. Ancient cave cellar—wine storage since Hellenistic times (2,000+ years); 15–16°C year-round temperature. Koralli (red/white), Kelaidonis (red/white/rosé), Mayoklima Merlot. Museum with old tools. Tastings €5 with olives, bread, cheese platters. 9:30–18:00 in season; call ahead Nov–Mar.

The Commandaria Museum in Silikou celebrates one of Cyprus's oldest and most famous sweet wines. Historic village, 650 metres altitude, stone presses and exhibits. The museum explains how Commandaria grapes were sun-dried and vinified using traditional methods. Also displays olive-oil equipment and household items. Silikou sits in the heart of the Commandaria zone; the Savvas winery is nearby. Contact the village before you go to confirm opening hours and whether tastings are available.

HCH Winery is a family-run boutique in the heart of Stroumbi village. Handmade, limited-production wines—around 2,000 bottles a year—from their own vineyards. Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah. Hands-on experiences: grape smashing, juice tasting, bottle filling. The setting in the Paphos hills enhances the tasting. Book ahead; they run a lean operation and appreciate the notice. Winter tastings in the stone-built space feel intimate.

A family passion project in the Pitsilia mountains. Fanis Pittalis returned to his ancestral village and rescued forgotten vineyards. His great-grandfather planted vines in 1910; today Pittali honours that legacy with small-scale winemaking that balances tradition and innovation. Old and new vineyards. Book ahead; they run a lean operation. The Pitsilia light in winter is sharp. Combine with Madari Ridge or Kyperounta for a full mountain day.

Boutique winery in Vasa Koilaniou, Krasochoria village. Mavro, Maratheftiko, Xynisteri, plus international varieties. Their grand stone cellar was built by local masons. Relaxed, welcoming atmosphere; staff speak English, Russian, Greek. Call ahead Nov–Mar. The Petra white and red blends showcase local varieties. Groups welcome. Vasa sits between Omodos and Koilani—easy to combine with a full Krasochoria loop.

Commandaria pioneers on the Laona border. Karseras helped revive modern Commandaria production. Traditional sun-dried grapes, barrel ageing. The tasting room is cosy; the story of how they brought Commandaria back to the fore is worth hearing. Near Platres; combine with a morning trail. Call ahead in winter. Their Commandaria stands up to the best.

Where tradition meets the future. Evangelou sits in Pera Pedi—Krasochoria village with Commandaria tradition. Indigenous varieties, modern techniques. Their Commandaria-style wines and dry offerings attract visitors who want both heritage and quality. The tasting room is warm; book ahead in winter. Combine with Omodos, Koilani, or Hadjipavlou for a full village circuit.

The monastery's own winery, distinct from the Chrysorrogiatissa monastery attraction. Winemaking here dates to 1725; the facility reopened in 1984. Indigenous Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Mavro, plus Shiraz and Cabernet. The spiritual setting—within the monastery grounds—complements the tasting. Book ahead. Panayia village is nearby. Combine with Vouni Panayia winery and the Laona route for a full Paphos hills day.

Established 1943—Cyprus's first public company in wine. LOEL invested in a state-of-the-art winery at Ayios Silas in 2020, producing fine wines from indigenous varieties. They support local growers with annual grape purchases. Modern facility, heritage brand. Tastings and tours; book ahead. Easy access from Limassol. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or Zambartas for a coastal–vineyard day.

Cyprus's oldest winemaker—since 1844. Christodoulos Haggipavlu started the commercial wine business; six generations later, ETKO runs Olympus Winery in Omodos. Commandaria, Cabernet (Ino), Maratheftiko, Xynisteri. Modern plant and equipment, research into new wines. The Omodos facility welcomes visitors. Book ahead. Do the monastery and village first; ETKO completes the Omodos story.

Small-batch Commandaria in Agios Mamas. Traditional methods, sun-dried grapes, time in the barrel. Revecca is one of the quieter names on the Commandaria route—fewer visitors, more room to talk. Call ahead; they run a lean operation. Agios Mamas village sits in the heart of the zone. Combine with Karseras, Savvas, or Silikou Museum for a full Commandaria day.

KEO's historic winery since 1927, at the entrance to Mallia village. Fifty hectares of estate vineyards, major production hub, and research centre for indigenous grape revival. Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi, Xynisteri, Commandaria St. John. Tours and tastings; book ahead. The scale is industrial but the story is Cypriot—KEO helped put Cypriot wine on the map. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or a coastal drive.

Boutique winery near the Commandaria zone. Small production, quality focus. Their wines sit between tradition and modern craft. Call ahead; they welcome visitors who appreciate the small scale. Souni is off the main Krasochoria loop—fewer crowds, more conversation. Combine with Omodos, Kolossi, or a Limassol coast day.

Traditional Cypriot wines since the early 20th century. Commandaria—their Nama carries the ancient name, aged in oak for over ten years. Kastelani Red and White from indigenous Mavro and Xynisteri. Special Reserve aged in French oak. Sparkling by the Champagne method. Mandria village, near the Commandaria zone. Tours and tastings; book ahead. Heritage in every bottle.

Coastal Limassol winery. Vineyards near the sea; a different terroir from the mountains. Crisp whites, easy-drinking reds. Tours and tastings; book ahead. Combine with a beach morning at Governor's Beach or a Kourion afternoon. Twenty minutes from Limassol. Winter tastings with sea views.

Small family winery in the Laona hills. Low-intervention wines; Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Mavro. The tasting room is intimate. Call ahead—they welcome visitors who appreciate the craft. Pano Panayia village; Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery nearby. Combine with the monastery, Vouni Panayia winery, or a Laona loop. Winter: cosy and unhurried.

Family winery in the heart of Krasochoria. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Commandaria. The village of Koilani has ten wineries; Lambouri holds its own. Cosy tasting room. Book ahead. Combine with Omodos, Lania, or a full Krasochoria loop. Winter: heaters, mountain views, unhurried tastings.

current.openingHours: By appointment; book ahead for tours. Call ahead Nov–Mar.
current.description: Historic cooperative since 1943. One of Cyprus's largest; the story of Cypriot wine in one place. Tours of the facility, tastings, shop. Industrial scale but heritage heart. Limassol seafront. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or a city explore. Winter: fewer crowds, full tours available.

Nicosia district winery. Vineyards in the Mesaoria and foothills. Modern approach, indigenous and international varieties. Tasting room; book ahead. Combine with Lefkara, Machairas, or a Nicosia hinterland day. Winter: quiet, focused tastings. About 40 minutes from the capital.

Larnaca wine route. Commandaria focus; sweet and semi-sweet. The village setting is peaceful. Book ahead. Combine with Stavrovouni, Choirokoitia, or Zygi for fish. Winter: ideal for Commandaria tastings. The Larnaca hills have their own microclimate.

Boutique Nicosia winery. Small production, quality focus. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko. The tasting experience is intimate. Call ahead. Combine with Agros, Machairas, or Kalopanagiotis for a mountain day. Winter: cosy, personal. Off the main wine routes—discovery territory.

Pitsilia wine route. High-altitude vineyards; crisp whites, structured reds. Family-run. The drive up is scenic. Book ahead. Combine with Kykkos, Pedoulas, or Troodos trails. Winter: can be cooler at elevation; the tasting room warms you. Authentic mountain wine.

Larnaca hills winery. Modern facility, indigenous varieties. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi. Tastings and tours; book ahead. Combine with Lefkara, Stavrovouni, or the Larnaca coast. Winter: mild in the hills. A different side of Cypriot wine.

Family winery on the Limassol wine route. Traditional and modern. Commandaria, dry whites, reds. Cosy tasting. Book ahead. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or Omodos. Winter: heaters, unhurried. The Limassol corridor has many options; Zambeli is a quiet favourite.

Troodos foothills. Near Platres; combine with Caledonia Falls or Artemis. Small production, mountain character. Xynisteri, reds. Call ahead. Winter: the mountains are the draw; a winery stop adds depth. Cosy tasting room.

Vouni village, Krasochoria. Boutique production. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Commandaria. The village is quiet; the winery welcomes visitors who book. Combine with Omodos, Lania, or Silikou. Winter: peaceful, personal. A hidden Krasochoria stop.

Historic village of Fikardou; UNESCO heritage. The wine estate complements the restored stone houses. Small production; book ahead. Combine with the village walk, Machairas, or Agros. Winter: the village is magical; snow possible. A culture and wine day.

Kathikas village, Akamas edge. On the Laona–Akamas wine route. Combine with Adonis, Aphrodite, or The Farmyard for lunch. Boutique; Xynisteri, Maratheftiko. Book ahead. Winter: the Akamas loop; trail in the morning, wine and lunch after. Coastal-meets-mountain.

Between Larnaca and Limassol. No ruins, no lace. Just fish. The tavernas line the harbour; they serve what the boats brought in that morning. Locals eat here. Winter lunch on the waterfront—octopus, sea bream, calamari. The pace is slow. The coffee after is obligatory. Zygi is where Cypriots go for Sunday fish. Combine with Choirokoitia, Lefkara, or Cape Greco trail.

White cliffs above dark volcanic sand. The tavernas perch on the cliffs; they serve fresh fish and meze. On a mild December afternoon you can sit outside with a blanket. The fish is fresh, the wine flows. One of the best winter lunch spots on the coast. The contrast—white cliffs, dark sand—is striking in winter light. Combine with Kourion or Kolossi in the morning, fish at lunch. Cape Greco trail or Choirokoitia are within reach for a full day.

Wiz 50 Best #1 for 2025. Mediterranean fine dining at Alasia Boutique Hotel. Executive chef Pavlos Kyriakis. Balanced flavours, impeccable technique, exceptional service. Reserve ahead; dress smart. Winter evenings are cosy. A special-occasion spot for discerning travellers.

Wiz 50 Best top 5. Ethnic Asian comfort cuisine in Kathikas, Paphos. Head Chef Savvas Iakovides. Farm-to-table ethos. On the Akamas loop—do Adonis or Aphrodite in the morning, then book lunch. The village setting and the food make it a destination. Reserve ahead; it fills. Winter: trail in the morning, this meal as the reward.

The taverna by the river. The owner knows every hiker. Order the trout with almonds—psaróvrasto, poached in wine and herbs. The fireplace, the mountain air, the sound of the Kryos Potamos. It's the pairing locals do after Artemis or Caledonia Falls. Do the trail in the morning; finish by 1pm. Drive to Platres. Don't skip it.

current.openingHours: Tavernas typically 12–15:30, 19–23; some close Mon or Tue
current.description: Post-Adonis or Aphrodite trail. The harbour tavernas serve fish that's fresh—what the boats brought in. Vasilikon winery is on the Akamas loop back. Or skip the wine and just eat. The trail earns you the meal. Polis knows how to feed hikers. Harbour views, relaxed pace. No high-rises, no neon—just fish, wine, and the bay.

Wiz 50 Best #2. International casual fine dining. French-inspired cuisine with Mediterranean fusion by Chef Christodoros Theofanou. Award-winning. Winter terrace when it's mild. Reserve ahead. A notch below The Polo in formality but top-tier in execution.

Wiz 50 Best top 5. Mediterranean cuisine in Nicosia. Contemporary, creative. Rainy-day Nicosia escape. Combine with the Leventis Museum or a stroll through the old town. Reserve ahead. A capital-city option when the coast or mountains don't call.

River setting. Psaróvrasto—trout poached in wine and herbs. Kakopetria's trout tavernas line the Kryos Potamos. Do Caledonia Falls, Kryos Potamos loop, or Kampos tou Livadiou in the morning; Kakopetria for lunch. The village knows hikers. Fireplace, mountain air, the sound of the river. Winter: cosy inside.

Winery lunch with sea views. Santo perches above Limassol; the restaurant stays open year-round. On a mild winter day you can sit outside with a blanket. Their Ayios Onoufrios red pairs with Cypriot meze. Ask for a wine-paired lunch. Heaters in winter. Sunset in December around five.

current.openingHours: Cafés and tavernas; typically 9–18 or lunch hours
current.description: Ruins over your shoulder. Kouklia village sits beside Palaipafos, the ancient sanctuary of Aphrodite. The village cafés and tavernas offer simple Cypriot fare with a view of history. Coffee, meze, a slow lunch. Winter is quiet; the site and the village belong to those who take their time. Combine Palaipafos in the morning, Kouklia for lunch. Petra tou Romiou coastal path is nearby.

Wiz 50 Best #2 for 2025. Ethnic Asian cuisine at Four Seasons Hotel, Limassol. Cantonese-based cuisine under Head Chef Guan Ruijiong. Winter menu and terrace. Reserve ahead. A notch of sophistication for special evenings. Combine with Kourion or Kolossi for a coastal day, then dinner.

Post-Angeloktisti church. The Byzantine church of Angeloktisti in Kiti draws visitors; the village tavernas do lunch. Simple Cypriot fare, meze, village pace. Church first—the 6th-century mosaic is one of the oldest in the eastern Mediterranean—then lunch. Combine with Zygi for fish or Lefkara for lace. Larnaca Salt Lake and Cape Greco are within reach.

The trout tavernas of Platres. Order psaróvrasto—trout poached in wine and herbs. Fireplace, mountain air, the sound of the Kryos Potamos. After Artemis, Caledonia, or Kampos tou Livadiou. The village knows hikers. Psilo Dendro is the classic; others line the river. Winter lunch by the fire.

Harbour fish on the Akamas edge. Latsi serves what the boats bring in—simpler than Polis, closer to the Baths of Aphrodite trailhead. Winter lunch by the water. Combine with Adonis, Aphrodite, or Smigies in the morning; Latsi for lunch before the loop back. The drive along the coast is part of the day. Less crowded than Polis harbour.

Laiki Geitonia and the old town. Tavernas tucked in cobbled streets. Meze, souvlaki, halloumi. Winter evenings are cosy. Combine with Leventis Museum, Cyprus Museum, or a rainy-day capital explore. The old town has a different rhythm. Reserve for popular spots.

Cliff tavernas above Pissouri Bay. Sunset views over the curve of the coast. Meze, fish, local wine. Winter sunsets around five. The bay stays mild when the mountains are cold. Combine with Petra tou Romiou coastal path, Kourion ruins, or Avakas Gorge. A west-Limassol lunch or dinner.

current.openingHours: Tavernas typically 12–15:30, 19–22; square cafés all day
current.description: The cobbled square of Omodos. Tavernas under the plane trees. Meze, kleftiko, halloumi, local wine. After a Krasochoria winery loop—Tsiakkas, Oenou Yi, Lania, Loukas—or the Artemis trail, Omodos is the natural lunch stop. The monastery overlooks the village. Winter sun on the square. The pace is slow. Reserve on weekends.

current.openingHours: Most venues 10–23; some close 22. Varies by restaurant—check individual listings.
current.description: Superyachts. Cobbled promenade. The marina sits between the old town and the sea—Mediterranean, fish, Italian, sushi. In winter the crowds thin and the light on the water is golden. The cafés and restaurants stay open; sit outside with a blanket on mild December evenings. This is urban Cyprus at its best. Not the villages—the city pulse, the marina buzz, the promenade stroll. Reserve for waterfront tables; the popular spots fill. Pair with Kolossi or Kourion in the morning, then come here for dinner. The contrast hits.

Protaras waterfront and inland. Fish tavernas by the sea; village meze spots. Winter: fewer crowds, mild evenings. Do the Cape Greco trail in the morning, Protaras for lunch. Fig Tree Bay and Konnos are nearby. The pace is slower than summer. Reserve for popular spots.

Larnaca seafront and old town. Meze, fish, souvlaki. The Finikoudes promenade and the backstreets. Winter: mild; sit outside with a blanket. Combine with Salt Lake, Kiti, Choirokoitia, or Zygi. The city has its own rhythm.
Pafos harbour and castle area. Fish, meze, harbour views. Winter sunsets. Combine with Pafos mosaics, Tomb of Kings, or Coral Bay. The castle lights up at dusk. Reserve for waterfront spots.

Agros village. Rose products, loukoumi, mountain meze. The village is famous for roses and sweets. Tavernas serve local fare. Combine with Machairas Forest trail, Xyliatos Dam, or the Kykkos road. Winter: cosy, mountain character. Rose liqueur and loukoumi before or after lunch.

current.openingHours: Tavernas typically 12–15:30, 19–22; some close Mon or Tue
current.description: The lace village. UNESCO-recognised Lefkaritiko since the Venetians. Tavernas in stone buildings, silver workshops, lacemakers in doorways. Meze, local wine, village pace. Pano and Kato Lefkara—two villages, one tradition. Winter light on the cobbles; fewer tour buses; the craft comes first.

Kathikas village on the Akamas loop. Traditional tavernas; meze, local wine. The Farmyard is the star—book ahead; others offer simpler fare. Combine with Adonis, Aphrodite, or Smigies in the morning; Kathikas for lunch. Vasilikon and Sygkrasi wineries are minutes away. Winter: trail in the morning, village lunch after.
Limassol old town and Saripolou Square. Tavernas, meze, souvlaki. The castle area. Winter: mild; the old town has a different pulse. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or the marina. Urban Cyprus.

Kyrenia harbour. Fish tavernas with castle views. The harbour is the heart. Winter: milder than the mountains; harbour stroll, fish lunch. Note: access from south Cyprus; check current routes. Combine with Bellapais, St Hilarion.

Ayia Napa beyond the clubs. Village square tavernas, harbour fish spots. Winter: the resort quietens; authentic Cypriot dining emerges. Combine with Sea Caves, Cape Greco, Nissi Beach. The off-season reveals another side.

current.openingHours: Visitor centre and cafés; typically 9–17 or 18
current.description: Troodos Square and the visitor centre area. Cafés, simple lunches, hot chocolate. After Artemis, Atalante, or Persephone. Winter: essential post-hike warmth. Snow possible; the square is the hub. Not fancy—coffee, sandwiches, warmth. The mountains do the work; Troodos Square restores you.

Solea Valley villages—Kakopetria, Galata, Kalopanagiotis. Trout, meze, mountain fare. River settings, fireplaces. Combine with Mylikouri trail, Kampos tou Livadiou, Kryos Potamos, or Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis. Winter: the valley is cosy. Psaróvrasto (trout) is the classic.

Zygi's smaller marina and back-street spots. Less touristy than the main harbour. Fresh fish, meze. Winter Sunday lunch—locals' ritual. Combine with Choirokoitia, Lefkara, or Governor's Beach. The pace is slow.

Episkopi village near Kourion. Tavernas with views of the ancient site. Meze, local wine. Do Kourion ruins in the morning; Episkopi for lunch. Combine with Kolossi, Governor's Beach, or Zambartas winery. Winter: mild; the ruins glow in afternoon light. The theatre faces the sea.

Winter Troodos favorite. Seven-kilometre loop around Chionistra (Mount Olympus) at about 1,850 m through Troodos National Forest Park. Black pine, golden oak, ridge views. Forestry Department grade 1—smooth path, little climb. In winter the air is crisp, the crowds thin. Well-marked; weather changes fast—pack layers.

Best winter waterfall hike. Official Forestry route is about 3 km linear between Troodos (above) and Psilo Dentro above Pano Platres, along Kryos Potamos. Grade 2–3: stream crossings, slippery stones. Flow peaks in late winter; forest green, air cool. Waterproof boots. Ask in Platres about rainfall.

Full Troodos day hike. Official Forestry Atalanti Trail is a 14 km loop from Troodos Square around Chionistra, lower than Artemis—dense black pine and Troodos juniper (including an ~800-year-old specimen). Grade 2; about five hours. Drinking water about 3 km in; old chromium mine entrance near 5 km. Cross the Troodos–Prodromos road near 9 km and follow signs back to the square. Start early; pack lunch.

Short Troodos classic. Official Persephone Trail runs about 3 km from near Troodos Square (police station side, ~1,720 m) to the Makria Kontarka viewpoint (~1,660 m)—linear, so return the same way or via the signed forest road. Grade 1. Dense black pine, endemic flora signs, views toward Limassol vineyards and Cape Gata on clear days. Quieter than Artemis.

Cyprus's highest peak. 1,952 metres. Winter: snow and ice common Jan–Mar. Microspikes needed. Steep ascent through black pine; 360-degree view on clear days. Start early; cloud builds by midday. Check conditions. Ski resort café at trailhead.

Winter Akamas favorite. Official Forestry Adonis Trail is about 7.5 km circular from the Baths of Aphrodite (grade 2, ~3 hours). Shares the first ~2.5 km with Aphrodite toward Pyrgos tis Rigainas, then continues via Kefalovrysia and Queen's Tower. Rocky and uphill early. December and January: ideal temps. Combine with Vasilikon (Akamas loop) or Chrysorrogiatissa and Kolios (Paphos hills).

Official Forestry Aphrodite Trail is about 7.5 km circular from the Baths of Aphrodite (grade 2, ~3 hours). Shares the early stretch with Adonis, then climbs toward Moutti tis Sotiras with Chrysochou Bay views. Winter is ideal—mild coast, wildflowers Feb–Mar. Pack a wind layer for the ridge.

Avakas Gorge is a slot in the limestone. Official Forestry route is about 1.2 km linear into the gorge (grade 1–2, allow ~2 hours with care). Walls rise high on either side; river crossings and slip risk. Centauria akamantis grows here. Do not go after heavy rain—flash floods are real. December–April when the river is manageable. Waterproof boots; some scrambling.

Official Forestry outside-forest route: 1.2 km linear, about 30 minutes, grade 3. Between Platres church and the village centre—or via a dirt road from the Platres–Limassol road near Psilo Dentro. Rich vegetation along Kryos River; opens to garrigue with views south. The waterfall is the tallest in Troodos (~20 m). Steeper and rougher than the boardwalk suggests—watch footing after rain.

The Horteri Trail is the one for experienced hikers. Nine kilometres through Troodos forest. Steep sections, rocky terrain, long stretches of solitude. You climb, dip, and climb again. The reward is views and silence. In winter, snow can settle on the higher points from January to March. Microspikes are often essential. Start early. Tell someone your route. The forest swallows you. Phone signal is patchy. But if you're fit and prepared, Horteri delivers. You'll earn your village lunch.

Six kilometres along the Cape Greco coast. Sea caves, limestone cliffs, coves where the water shifts from turquoise to deep blue. In winter the sun is mild and the path is quiet. No snow, no crowds. The trail is well-marked. You can start at the Cape Greco car park or at Konnos Bay. The sea is always on one side. The light changes with the hour. Bring a wind layer; the cliffs funnel the breeze. It's the kind of hike that feels like a gift: easy underfoot, views that don't quit. Combine with a swim in summer or a coffee at Konnos in winter.

The long route. Eleven kilometres from Platres to Troodos, passing Caledonia Falls along the way. You walk the length of the Kryos Potamos valley; the Cold River; through forest that feels ancient. The waterfall is the midpoint. Stop. Rest. Then push on. It's a point-to-point hike, so you need transport at both ends. Arrange a car or a lift. Allow six hours. Muddy sections after rain. Snow possible at the Troodos end in deep winter. Start early. Pack lunch. This is a full day in the mountains. Fit hikers only. But if you're up for it, the Caledonia Long Route is one of the island's best walks.

Eight kilometres along the Madari Ridge. When the day is clear, 360° views over Pitsilia and Troodos. The fire watchtower marks the high point. Pine forest, open ridges, a stretch of the E4 long-distance trail. In winter the ridge can be windy. Snow sometimes settles in January and February. Check the forecast. On clear days the coast stretches out. A misty one still has its atmosphere; the forest closes in, the tower emerges from the cloud. Allow four or five hours. Bring layers. The ridge exposes you.

A coastal walk that strings together one of Cyprus's most famous landmarks; Petra tou Romiou, Aphrodite's Rock; with quiet stretches of shoreline. You start near the viewpoint car park and follow paths and tracks that keep the sea in sight. In winter the light is softer, the crowds gone. Waves break on the rocks, the air smells of salt and wild thyme. The route is mostly easy underfoot, with one or two short climbs to low bluffs for better views along the coast toward Pissouri. It's a half-day option when the mountains feel too cold. Pair it with a village lunch inland or a visit to Kourion or the Pafos mosaics to round out the day.

Official Forestry Smigies Trail offers short (~2.5 km / 1 h) and long (~7.5 km / 3 h) circular routes from Smigies picnic site (grade 2). Long route is the default here—Peana lookout, Lara and Chrysochou Bay views, connection with Adonis at Kefalovrysia. Abandoned magnesium kilns along the way. Winter temps ideal. Combine with Vasilikon or Sterna and Polis for lunch.

Forest station trail in the heart of Akamas. Stavros tis Psokas is a forestry outpost; the trail winds through pine and scrub with wildlife spotting opportunities—mouflon, if you're lucky. Remote, quieter than the Baths of Aphrodite area. Winter brings crisp air and fewer visitors. Allow two to three hours. The drive in is part of the adventure; rough in places. Combine with Polis or Latsi for a coastal lunch on the way back.

Official Forestry circular: 3 km, about 1.5 hours, grade 1. Cliff-edge views of Chromium River, Solea Valley, Morphou Bay, and the tip of Chionistra through black pine and century-old junipers. First kilometre shared with Mnimata Piskopon. Endemic flora signs (Cyprus skullcap, Troodos Alyson, golden oak). Natura 2000 Troodos National Forest Park. Quiet winter leg-stretcher; picnic site nearby.

Official Akamas circular from Smigies picnic site: 3 km, about 2 hours, Forestry grade 2. Climb to Pissouromoutti hill (about 400 m), then circle down. Views south to Lara and Geronisos, north over Chrysochou Bay. Juniper, lentisk, pine shade on warm days. Year-round; drinking water at the picnic site. Mythology ties the name to Adonis and Aphrodite’s night chase.

A section of the E4 European Long Distance Walk. From Platres through forest to the Caledonia Falls area. Pine, golden oak, mountain views. The E4 crosses Cyprus from coast to coast; this segment gives a taste of long-distance hiking. Allow four hours. Winter: check conditions; can be snowy at higher points. Combine with Platres for lunch or a second shorter trail.

The Humming of the Bees. A 2.5 km nature path in Agioi Vavatsinias village, Larnaca uplands. Bee-themed: bee-friendly plants, decorative beehives, bee hotels. Hexagonal wooden pavilions and benches. Educational and restorative. Suitable for all fitness levels. Winter is quiet; the village sits at 700m. Combine with Lefkara, Stavrovouni, or Choirokoitia for a full Larnaca hinterland day.

Official Forestry outside-forest circular: 9.8 km, about 3 hours, grade 3 from Pano Panagia (below the church, opposite the Cultural Center). Vineyards, Natura 2000 site of Vouni Panagias, and views of Akamas, Paphos Forest, and Troodos. Optional detour to Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery or a shorter return to the village. Fire lookout station access at Vouni.

Official Forestry linear: 8 km, about 3 hours, grade 3. Starts near Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (first km shared with that circular); mostly downhill from ~1,700 m to ~980 m. Cliff-edge views of Chromium River, Solea Valley, Morphou Bay, and Chionistra. Black pine gives way to Calabrian pine below 1,400 m. Ends on the Platania–Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis forest road—continue to Kakopetria or Platania. Natura 2000. Arrange transport.

The Cold River valley. A forest walk along the Kryos Potamos, the stream that feeds Caledonia Falls. Less demanding than the full Caledonia Long Route; good for a half-day in the mountains. Pine, moss, the sound of water. Winter brings crisp air. Can be combined with a shorter visit to the falls. Platres for lunch. Start from Psilo Dendro or the Caledonia trailhead.

Official Forestry linear: 2.5 km, about 1 hour, grade 2. Valley of the Eagles between about 1,110 m and 1,010 m. Smooth path through pine forest near Amiantos; river crossings when water is up. Short characterful leg-stretcher. Arrange transport for the linear route.

Easy loop in the Limassol hills. The trail passes the church of Panagia tis Amasgou and winds through olive groves and scrub. Gentle grade; family-friendly. Winter sun, mild temps. Combine with Monagri, Omodos, or a Krasochoria winery visit. A relaxed morning or afternoon option.

Circular route through the Adelfoi forest. Views of Xyliatos Dam and surrounding mountains. Easy grade; suitable for all. About 50 minutes from Nicosia. Winter brings crisp air and fewer visitors. The ascending start is the hardest section; the rest rewards with dam and forest views. Picnic area at the trailhead. Combine with Kakopetria or Agros for a Nicosia hinterland day.

Forest trail in the Troodos heartland. Pine, ridges, mountain views. Moderate grade; allow two and a half hours. Winter can bring snow at elevation; check conditions. Connects to the wider Troodos trail network. Platres or Kakopetria for lunch. A solid half-day in the mountains.

Forest trail around Machairas Monastery. Pine and golden oak; mountain views. The monastery sits at 870m. The trail winds through the surrounding forest. Moderate grade; allow three hours. Winter: crisp air, fewer visitors. Combine with the monastery, Agros, or a Nicosia hinterland day. About an hour from Nicosia. The monastery café does a good post-hike coffee.

Extended loop in the Troodos forest, north of Platres. Pine, streams, mountain quiet. Slightly longer than the short Horteri option. Good for a half-day when you want more than a leg-stretcher but less than Artemis. Winter: check conditions; can be cool at elevation. Platres for trout after. Combine with Caledonia Falls or Kampos tou Livadiou for a full mountain day.

Dramatic gorge in the Paphos forest. Rocky terrain, endemic flora. Allow four hours. Winter: cooler, ideal for hiking. The gorge narrows in places; spectacular. Combine with Polis, Latsi, or the Akamas trails. Point-to-point; arrange transport. One of Cyprus's finest gorge walks.

Official wheelchair-accessible circular: 1.5 km, about 30 minutes, grade 1. Gravel path through black pine and juniper near Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (not Troodos Square). Viewpoint over Chromium River and Solea Valley; century-old trees; flora signs. Natura 2000. Ideal for families and first-timers.

Forest trail near Kakopetria. Pine, streams, mountain air. Moderate grade. Allow two hours. Winter: crisp; often clear. Combine with Kakopetria trout tavernas, Kampos tou Livadiou, or Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis. A Solea Valley classic.

Extended variant of the Persephone trail. More distance, more forest. Troodos heartland. Moderate grade. Allow nearly three hours. Winter: check conditions; can be cool. Platres for lunch. Connects to the wider Troodos network.

Short loop through golden oak and black pine. Easy grade; one hour. Endemic flora. Family-friendly. Winter: often clear; good for a gentle morning. Combine with Platres, Kykkos road, or other Troodos trails.

Official Forestry outside-forest linear: 2.5 km, about 1 hour, grade 3 (descending). Connects Pano Lefkara with Kato Drys through rural paths with views in all directions. Links to the Lefkara–Metamorfoseos church trail. Lace villages and stone paths—culture with a proper downhill workout.

Circular route around Potamia Dam. Water views, birdlife, gentle grade. Easy; suitable for all. About 40 minutes from Nicosia. Winter: mild; good for a capital escape. Combine with Agros, Machairas, or Nicosia old town.

Forest trail in the Troodos. Pine, ridges. Moderate grade. Allow two and a half hours. Winter: crisp; check conditions. Combine with Platres, Caledonia, or Kampos tou Livadiou. A solid half-day option.

Historic trail; the name recalls a darker past. Today: forest, mountain air, Troodos character. Moderate grade. Allow nearly three hours. Winter: crisp; can be cool. Platres or Kakopetria for lunch. Part of the Troodos narrative.

Alternative approach to the Caledonia Falls area. Different start; same waterfall reward. Forest, stream, cooler temps. Allow two hours. Winter: muddy sections possible; waterproof boots. Platres for lunch.

Foothills of the Five Fingers mountain. Views of the coast and the range. Easy grade. Note: access from south Cyprus; check current routes. Combine with Bellapais, St Hilarion, or coastal Kyrenia. Winter: mild on the coast; the mountains frame the view.

Flat circuit around Larnaca Salt Lake. Flamingos in winter; Hala Sultan Tekke mosque; birdlife. Easy, flat. Allow two hours. Winter: ideal for flamingos. Combine with Larnaca town, Kiti, or the airport corridor. A coastal wetlands escape.

The king of winter trails. A seasonal lake appears only after heavy rain or snow—few know it exists. The route passes an abandoned asbestos mine with lunar-like terrain, then descends to the secret lake. Go anticlockwise to reach the lake earlier. Best in winter when Troodos is dusted with snow. Go with someone who knows the route; it's hiker-made, not officially marked.

Abandoned village, Venetian bridge, ruined watermill. Vretsia was evacuated after 1974; the trail feels like walking through an open museum. The Roudias bridge over the Xeros River is the jewel—stone arches, cool shade, lush vegetation. Circular route: start from Vretsia, follow the gravel road to the bridge, return via the trail. Remote Paphos forest. Winter brings crisp air and solitude.

Official Forestry linear: 8 km downhill in about 1 hour, grade 2 (1,315–1,050 m). Historic path villagers used toward the Amiantos asbestos mine. Starts ~300 m from Chrysovrysi stone fountain on the Karvounas–Troodos road—fill bottles before you go. Dense Calabrian pine, golden oak, gabbro of the Troodos ophiolite; last stretch on a dirt farm road into Amiantos. Natura 2000. Arrange transport at Amiantos.

Official Cape Greco circular: 1.2 km, about 45 minutes, grade 1. Starts at the old quarry car park; slight climb to Kavos hill then loop down. Pine then juniper and lentisk scrub; panoramic views to Pedalio lighthouse, Agia Napa, and the south cliffs (rock climbing). Connects to Sea Caves–Agioi Anargyroi. Year-round winter sun option.

Peak of Winds. A hidden gem in the remote Paphos forest. Linear trail from Pano Panagia toward Stavros tis Psokas; shares a trailhead with Gefyria. Ridgeline walking, 360° views, fewer visitors than Troodos. The Paphos forest feels wilder—more untamed. Check GPS near the end; one junction can lead astray.

A hidden sanctuary. Gorge, stream, Grigoris Afxentiou hideout, Machairas Monastery. The path follows the Pediaios River through a vast ravine; a bridge halfway crosses the mountainside. Magical after rain—the stream runs strong, the forest turns vivid green. Linear; both ends accessible by car. Experienced hikers can extend to Lazanias or Fikardou.

Distinct from the rest of Cyprus. Kato Pyrgos area—abandoned village of Agios Theodoros, wooden bridge, gorge views, shimmering Mediterranean in the distance. The landscape rises sharply; it feels like Crete. Remote; reach via Nicosia or Paphos. Linear or circular. Winter brings crisp air. Totally worth the drive.
